messages:
Alice M: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a lightweight 'layered seed' approach for air-gapped installs. Goal: keep initial distro small and let operators pull delta layers when convenient.
BenC: tl;dr? why not stick with a single monolithic seed?
Alice M: Monolith is simple but huge (500MB+). Layered seed lets us ship a ~100MB base and optional model/artifact layers. Saves bandwidth for constrained customers.
Caroline: How do we ensure activation is atomic across layers? if layer 3 fails, we can't leave the system half-applied.
Alice M: Plan: signed manifest with ordered layers + activation markers. Apply pipeline writes a tombstone+checkpoint before each layer. Activation only flips when final signature verification passes. If fail -> operator can rollback via recorded checkpoints.
SRE Lead: What's verifier memory/cpu cost for streaming-verify? customers care about resource-constrained onprem hosts.
Alice M: We stream-verify chunk-by-chunk using blake2b; verifier keeps a small rolling state (~2-4MB) not whole file. CPU cost is linear but parallelizable; we can throttle.
BenC: Operator UX? CLI examples?
Alice M: Example command: `rd-seed apply --source /mnt/usb --layers base,model-2026-02 --resume-token abc123`
Kyle: Does this need agent changes or is it purely packaging/orchestration?
Alice M: Minimal agent change: add resume-token and checkpoint API plus a small manifest verifier. Most logic lives in the operator CLI and the packaging tool.
Caroline: What about compatibility with existing offline verify tools and third-party signing HSM flows?
Alice M: Manifest signed by org key. We support detached-signature flow for HSMs (operator uploads sig separately). Verify code accepts detached sigs and an external root-of-trust bundle.
BenC: Edge-case: what if operator wants to reorder layers (e.g., apply model later)?
Alice M: Layers are independent, but base->runtime must be present. We allow out-of-order application for non-binding layers; manifest marks dependencies.
DevOps Bot: ci-packager: layered-seed build succeeded (size 112MB) :white_check_mark:
SRE Lead: Also add heuristics for backpressure during apply (disk full, network flakiness) — operator should be able to pause and resume safely.
Alice M: Agreed. We'll include `--pause`/`--resume` tokens and a safety timeout. All apply operations create a local operation journal for recovery.
BenC: Can we avoid extra complexity in the verifier by embedding incremental Merkle roots in the manifest? then rollback proofs are cheap.
Alice M: Yes — manifest will include per-layer merkle root + range proofs. That helps fast spot-checks and partial fetch proofs.
Caroline: Cool. Please drop an RFC PR with diagrams and a migration plan for existing customers.
Alice M: Will do — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/842 (draft). Feedback welcome, I'll iterate and post design doc in #architecture soon. :rocket:
